name: env-doctor
description: Doctor and janitor for your local dev environment. Diagnosis is read-only: MCP servers that will not load, spawn and encoding failures, 401 login loops, missing language servers or browsers, hooks that never fire, WSL networking, slow local services in WSL (measured file-I/O, Defender, memory, CPU and disk pressure), PowerShell argument traps and Syncthing conflicts; it routes a symptom to one branch, probes without changing anything and proposes one safe fix with no secrets printed. Cleaning is separate and gated: /env-doctor:clean inventories old databases, orphaned filestores, scratch folders, dead configs, caches and an oversized WSL disk image, and deletes only what you approve by plan id, with dumps before drops. Also: jobs over ~3 minutes run in the background (advisory hook), Windows script and Scheduled Task authoring, and a SessionStart check that speaks only on a real problem.

session_checks.title: Session start checks
session_checks.description: Run cheap read-only checks at session start (project .mcp.json, Syncthing ignores, low system-drive space, WSL disk-image bloat, a WSL version with a known crash) and report only problems.

long_job_advice.title: Long-job advice
long_job_advice.description: Before a Bash/PowerShell call that looks like a long job (full test suite, install/upgrade, dump/restore) running in the foreground, remind Claude to run it in the background and keep working. Advisory only, never blocks.
